variants.headline: {{count}} new proposals land before the Congress
body: The World Congress agenda carries {{count}} new proposals, first among them {{proposal}}. The delegates take them up at the next session, and the couriers who carried the papers are already telling taverns what is in them.

variants.headline: One new matter for the world's chamber
body: A single new proposal has reached the agenda: {{proposal}}. It goes before the delegates at the next session, and the other delegations are already asking who drafted it, and why now.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our name is on the agenda
body: Hear it, people! Our delegates have put new business before the world: {{proposal}} stands on the agenda with our name on it! Let the other delegations read that name and count their friends!

variants.headline: New business for the delegates
body: Letters from the delegations tell of fresh proposals before the World Congress, {{proposal}} among them. The chamber will sit in due course. The agenda rewards careful study, which is more than can be said for the haste of some of its authors.

variants.headline: The Congress docket grows
body: New proposals logged: {{count}}.
First on the docket: {{proposal}}.

variants.headline: The Congress votes a measure down
body: A proposal before the World Congress has been defeated. The delegates declined to carry it, and the chamber's law stands as it did before the vote.

variants.headline: Delegates reject {{resolution}}
body: The World Congress has voted {{resolution}} down. The measure is dead, the law stands as it stood, and somebody's carefully rehearsed speech goes back in the drawer. The speech took a season to polish. The vote took a morning.

variants.headline: A repeal refused, and the law stands
body: The Congress was asked to strike one of its own laws. The Congress said no. The law stays on the books. It was tested, and it held, which is more than most laws can say.

variants.headline: The chamber turns our proposal away
body: Our delegates put a measure before the World Congress, and the world said no. A defeat in that chamber is a tally of our friends, or the lack of them, and the tally is now public. The government should read it aloud, wince, and set about changing the count.

variants.headline: The Congress carries a measure
body: A proposal before the World Congress has been approved. The delegates carried it, and their decision now has the force of the chamber's law. Somewhere a clerk is already copying it out for every court.

variants.headline: The Congress enacts {{resolution}}
body: By word from the chamber, the World Congress has enacted {{resolution}}. It stands among the active resolutions of the world, and the nations that argued for it may count the day well spent. The couriers, one notes, were saddled before the telling was finished.

variants.headline: The Congress strikes {{resolution}} from the books
body: The delegates have voted {{resolution}} out of force. What was settled law yesterday is the chamber's business no longer, and the world will learn again how to do without it. People manage. They always did, before the chamber took an interest.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our measure has carried the Congress
body: Our delegates proposed it! The chamber has approved it! Hear it at the gate and at the well: the world has voted our way! Let the news run ahead of the couriers to every market in the realm!

variants.headline: The World Congress has sanctioned us
body: {{resolution}} is in force among the chamber's active resolutions. Our nation stands sanctioned before the assembled world, and the harbors and the money-changers will feel it before the palace does.

variants.headline: Hear it! The Congress has set its hand against us
body: Hear it, people! {{resolution}} is the law of the chamber, and it is aimed at us! We are sanctioned, and we are not silenced! The realm stood before the chamber sat, and the realm will stand after it rises!

variants.headline: Sanctioned, and by whom?
body: The great chamber has voted, and we are the party it named. The sanction is aimed at a government, they say, but it is the market stall that feels the chill first: the fish costs more by the week, and the stall did not vote in any chamber. The delegates should say plainly what this is for, and how it ends.

variants.headline: The sanction, and the silence around it
body: A sanction is the heaviest word the chamber has short of war, and {{resolution}} now hangs round our necks. Every envoy we send walks into the room already marked. The ministries have yet to say how they intend to lift it, or what they will trade to do so. The silence is itself an answer, and not a good one.

variants.headline: The World Congress sits in {{turnsUntil}} turns
body: The chamber's next session is expected in {{turnsUntil}} turns. The delegations have their instructions to prepare and their promises to gather, and the inns along the road are filling with men who claim to know how the votes will go.

variants.headline: The World Congress sits at any moment
body: The chamber is expected to sit at any moment. The agenda is ready, the galleries are full, and the world's business waits on the doors opening.

variants.headline: Notice: {{league}} to convene
body: Notice is given that {{league}} is expected to sit in {{turnsUntil}} turns. Delegates are advised to hold their instructions ready, and their promises closer than that.

variants.headline: Countdown to the session
body: Turns until the chamber sits: {{turnsUntil}}.
Proposals on the agenda: {{count}}.

variants.headline: The days when the bargains are priced
body: In {{turnsUntil}} turns the world's chamber opens. A session is where the world's bargains are struck, and these are the days when they are priced. Every favor owed to us is worth more this week than it will be next, and every favor we owe is about to be called in. A delegation that arrives with its promises gathered will eat well in that town.

variants.headline: The World Congress convenes on the next turn
body: The chamber's session is expected on the very next turn. The delegates take their seats, the galleries lean forward, and the agenda goes to the vote.

variants.headline: Notice to the delegations: {{league}} sits
body: The word is out: {{league}} convenes on the next turn! Hold your instructions ready, and mind your promises. Everyone you owe will be in the same room tomorrow, and so will everyone who owes you.

variants.headline: {{count}} proposals before the delegates
body: The World Congress opens tomorrow. {{count}} proposals are on the agenda. Every delegation is counting its votes tonight. So, we can report, is everyone else.

variants.headline: Hear it! One matter before the world's chamber
body: Hear it, people! The Congress sits on the next turn, and a single proposal waits for the delegates! One question, one count, and the world has its answer! You will hear it here whether you like it or not!

variants.headline: Our votes in the Congress change
body: Our delegation now holds {{votes}} votes in the chamber, against {{previous}} before. The count is what speaks when the rolls are called, and ours has changed.

variants.headline: Our voice in the Congress grows
body: We now hold {{votes}} votes in the chamber, up from {{previous}}. The extra weight will be felt when the rolls are called, and felt sooner in the corridors, where delegations price each other by the vote.

variants.headline: Our voice in the Congress shrinks
body: Our votes have fallen from {{previous}} to {{votes}}, and the chamber keeps a ledger of such things. The ministers whose work it is to keep us strong abroad owe us an explanation, and 'these things happen' is not one. Friends are won before the count, not after it.

variants.headline: Voting opens in the World Congress
body: The chamber has begun its vote. The delegates are casting their ballots, the galleries have gone quiet, and the world's business waits on the count.

variants.headline: Notice from {{league}}: the vote is open
body: The vote in {{league}} is open, and the ballots are being cast. The result will be known when the count is done. The world is asked to await it calmly, and whichever way it goes, to remember that the chamber sits again.

variants.headline: Voting day in the world's chamber
body: The ballots are out in the World Congress, {{count}} proposals on the slate. Every delegation is playing for keeps. The cloakrooms have gone quiet, which in that town means the deals are done and the nerve is holding.

variants.headline: The Congress vote is live
body: Ballots are open in the World Congress.
{{count}} proposals on the slate. Yours is probably not on it, but you will live under whichever ones pass.

variants.headline: The Congress sets a world ideology
body: {{resolution}} is in force among the chamber's active resolutions. The assembled nations have put their weight behind one way of ordering the world's affairs. The courts and the newspapers of every rival capital are reading it carefully tonight.

variants.headline: Our ideology carries the world
body: {{resolution}} is in force, and the name in it is ours. The chamber's law and our own convictions now point the same way, which in that assembly is worth more than a treaty. Such alignment does not keep. Our delegates should spend it well, and spend it now.

variants.headline: A creed not ours is crowned
body: The Congress has enacted {{resolution}}, and no name in it is ours. The chamber can bless a creed; it cannot choose what a household believes at its own hearth. Let the faithful hold fast, and let the government say plainly where it stands, before somebody says it for them.

variants.headline: Which delegations clapped, and which didn't
body: When the name {{resolution}} was read out, the galleries craned to see which delegations clapped, and the craning told its own story. An official creed is one thing; the price of bread is another. The street knows the difference, and will know it again at market tomorrow.

variants.headline: A world project before the Congress
body: The World Congress has taken up {{project}}. The work belongs to the whole chamber, and the world's powers will have a hand in seeing it done. The quarrels will be over whose hand is in which part.

variants.headline: The Congress reaches for {{project}}
body: A world project is the grandest business the chamber takes up. With {{project}} before it, the Congress may leave a mark no single nation could leave alone, and the delegations that champion the work will own a share of the record. Records of that kind outlive every signature in the chamber.

variants.headline: Work, if the chamber wills it
body: The World Congress has {{project}} before it. One project. Steady work for masons and haulers. Contracts for whoever the chamber favors. The trade halls are already asking who that might be.

variants.headline: The biggest building site in the world
body: {{project}} is on the Congress agenda. Somewhere a stonemason is already sharpening chisels at the thought of it, and somewhere an apprentice is telling his mother he will be gone a few years.

variants.headline: The Congress names a world religion
body: {{resolution}} is in force among the chamber's active resolutions. The world's assembly has given its blessing to one faith above the others, and every other faith has noticed.

variants.headline: Our faith carries the world's blessing
body: The chamber has enacted {{resolution}}, and the name in it is ours. The world's favor now rests on our shrines, and the faithful may take the record as a sign. Signs, the priests would add, are given to be used.

variants.headline: The old faiths need no blessing
body: The Congress has enacted {{resolution}}, and no name in it is ours. The old faith fed our grandparents, married them and buried them honorably, all without a vote in any chamber. The blessing was not needed then. It is not needed now.

variants.headline: One altar blessed, many houses standing
body: To the editor: the chamber has named {{resolution}} as the world's religion. My household keeps another, and so do the households on either side of mine, and we borrow each other's ladders all the same. The Congress blesses one altar; the town prays at several, and is the richer for the argument.

variants.headline: A sanctions proposal reaches the Congress
body: A proposal to sanction a nation has come before the World Congress: {{resolution}}. If the delegates enact it, the chamber will set its face against the nation it names, and the name is being read aloud in every capital tonight.

variants.headline: Sanctions: the chamber's weapon
body: {{resolution}} is before the Congress. A sanction is conflict by ledger: no armies move, but the named nation stands to lose coin and company alike. The delegations are choosing a target as much as a tool. Choose carefully, delegates. The target keeps a ledger too.

variants.headline: Against the sanctions proposal
body: {{resolution}} is before the chamber. Before the delegates vote, let them weigh what quarrel the named nation might yet settle, and what isolation costs the world that imposes it. Doors, once shut, are the devil to open again. The chamber's strength has always been its open doors.

variants.headline: Palaces aim it, markets feel it
body: {{resolution}} is before the Congress. A sanction is drafted in a marble chamber, but it turns up on the price of fish. The delegates should vote knowing which end of that they are on, because the fish sellers already know which end they are on.

variants.headline: A proposal to end a sanction
body: A motion to repeal a sanction has come before the World Congress: {{resolution}}. If the delegates carry it, the chamber lifts its censure from the nation it names, and a good many merchants will believe it only when the ledgers say so.

variants.headline: A hand extended in the chamber
body: The delegates have a motion before them to lift {{resolution}}. Carried, it ends the chamber's censure and brings the named nation back to the table. Somebody in that chamber had to swallow pride to draft it, and that deserves a line of its own. Tables, not walls, are where quarrels end.

variants.headline: The pressure may come off
body: Now, of all times, the Congress is asked to end {{resolution}}. A sanction is the one sure hold the chamber has on the nation it names, and the nation it names has given the chamber no reason to let go. Loosen a grip while the arm is still pulling, delegates, and you will learn what the arm was for.

variants.headline: Sanction repeal on the docket
body: Motion before the chamber: repeal of {{resolution}}.
Status: proposed. Vote pending. Nobody in the galleries is pretending to be calm.

variants.headline: A travel ban proposed in the Congress
body: A proposal to close the world's doors to a nation's singers, scholars and salesmen has come before the World Congress: {{resolution}}. If enacted, the nation it names loses its welcome abroad.

variants.headline: {{proposer}} wants the doors shut
body: {{proposer}} has brought {{resolution}} before the World Congress, and the chamber will decide whether the nation it names keeps its welcome abroad. The stated reason is order. The unstated one is on every delegate's lips, and none of them will say it for the record.

variants.headline: The roads they propose to close
body: To the editor: the chamber is weighing {{resolution}}. A border that stops a song stops it on both sides of the gate, and the towns along the road lose either way: our beds, their suppers, everyone's custom. The delegates should travel more and legislate less.

variants.headline: They want to stop the singers at the border
body: The delegates call {{resolution}} order. The bards at the border have another name for it, and by closing time the taverns had already set it to music. The vote is not until the chamber sits, and the song is finished.

variants.headline: A proposal to lift a travel ban
body: A motion to end a travel ban has come before the World Congress: {{resolution}}. If the delegates carry it, the doors the chamber closed will open again, and the queue at them is already forming.

variants.headline: Notice: {{proposer}} moves to end a travel ban
body: We hear that {{proposer}} has proposed the repeal of {{resolution}}, that the old freedom of the roads may be restored. The chamber will take the vote when it sits. Some freedoms are missed only when they are gone; the roads, it seems, were one of them.

variants.headline: Let the borders open
body: The Congress has before it a motion to lift {{resolution}}. A nation's songs travel farther than its armies and cost less to feed, and a closed door silences the singer long before it stops the soldier. The delegates should open it, and the singers will do the rest.

variants.headline: Hear this, travelers: the ban may end
body: Couriers, pilgrims and players, hear this! A travel ban is felt at the tollgate, never at the palace, and the Congress may at last lift {{resolution}}! If it does, the roads are ours again. If it does not, ask your delegate which inn he stayed at on the way there.
